\[
\sigma(f) = \sigma_{\max}\, \operatorname{smoothstep}\left(\frac{|f - f_c| - b}{w}\right),
\quad
I'(y) = (1 - \lambda)\, (G_{\sigma_k} * I)(y) + \lambda\, (G_{\sigma_{k+1}} * I)(y),
\qquad \sigma_k = \frac{k}{8}\, \sigma_{\max},\ \sigma_{\max} = 6
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(f, f_c\): The height of the row and of the focus center, as shares of the image
- \(b, w\): The half height of the sharp band and the transition
- \(\sigma_k\): The nine blur levels
- \(\lambda\): The blend weight of a row

f is the height of a row as a share of the image, f_c the focus center, b the half height of the sharp band and w the transition. Rows inside the band keep sigma 0. Outside it, sigma rises along a smoothstep to the largest blur. The image is blurred with Gaussians at nine sigmas, 0, 1/8 and so on up to the largest, each cut at 3 sigma. Each row blends the two blurred images whose sigmas lie around its own, with the weight lambda of its place between them. A real tilt-shift lens tilts its plane of focus. This filter only imitates the look, and its rule is PixelNexus's own.
